children: An apparent deceleration in Anthropic's revenue growth for the first three quarters of the year, as reported by WSJ and Financial Times, shouldn't be taken as a signal of faltering AI demand, D.A. Davidson's Gil Luria and Turner Dischinger say in a note. The slowdown may reflect OpenAI catching up as "this was the breakout quarter for open weight models," as well as growing use of open-weight models for less intensive or critical tasks. Though businesses are diversifying away from the two AI heavyweights, overall AI spending seems to be continuing on a steep upward trajectory, the analysts say. "This overall demand should support more AI compute demand and more data center construction, even if it doesn't meet the most outlandish extrapolations." (elias.schisgall@wsj.com)
